what_it_does: Modern chips are built from multiple smaller 'chiplets' (separate silicon dies) glued together, and each chiplet has its own local memory (called a cache) to hold data it needs quickly. When a chiplet needs data not in its own cache, it must fetch it across high-latency inter-die links, which is slow and costly. This paper tackles the challenge of finding the best combination of cache sizes, layouts, and inter-die connection strategies — a problem with an enormous number of possible configurations. The authors propose a two-level search algorithm: one level optimizes the caches within each chiplet, and the other optimizes the links between chiplets, iterating between the two until a good solution is found. The goal is to minimize a combined measure of average memory access time across all chiplets while staying within cost and power budgets.
